2B.19 Warnings against coming into unbelief.
3L.3 We should reprove and admonish one another to prevent sin.
Holy Ghost

precepts.text: Exhort one another daily, while it is called today, lest any of you be hardened through the deceitfulness of sin. Exhortation cannot happen if you are around nobody. Sin feels good but deceives; pull away and you may never recover. 2 Thessalonians 2:9-11: America came after the working of Satan with lying wonders; those who received not the love of the truth get strong delusion to believe a lie, still alive with a dead soul.
precepts.point: The kingdom is like leaven a woman hid in three measures of meal till the whole was leavened. Leaven grows.
precepts.why:
“But exhort one another daily, while it is called To day”. How often? Daily. Exhortation can't take place if you're not around nobody. The Bible is telling us what to do: stay around each other, stay around the righteous daily.

“lest any of you be hardened through the deceitfulness of sin”. Sin may feel good, but it's a deceiver, because you think you can get that feeling constantly. You can't; it's temporal, only for a certain amount of time. If we pull away, sin can take over our mind and we may never recover. That's the scary part.

2 Thessalonians 2 shows it. “Even him, whose coming is after the working of Satan with all power and signs and lying wonders”: America came after the workings of Satan, making you think God is with them, and it's time to come up out of the beast and separate. “And with all deceivableness of unrighteousness in them that perish; because they received not the love of the truth, that they might be saved.” They loved their pleasures more than God, deceived by the pleasures of sin. “And for this cause God shall send them strong delusion”. You can be deceived by sin so bad you may never recover your soul: still alive, still living, but a dead soul and a dead spirit. Be very mindful.

precepts.text: Consider the Apostle and High Priest of our profession, Christ Jesus; the work of the Lord is the profession of the called.
precepts.point: The work of the Lord is the true calling over any occupation held in Babylon: consider the Apostle and High Priest of our profession, Christ Jesus; fight the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life, whereunto thou art also called, and hast professed a good profession before many witnesses.
precepts.why:
Pharaoh said, “Let there more work be laid upon the men, that they may labour therein; and let them not regard vain words.” The same tactic runs in this captivity: burdens are increased and extra wages dangled for working the Sabbath and the feast days, to wear the people down so they will not regard the words of the Most High.

“Wherefore, holy brethren, partakers of the heavenly calling, consider the Apostle and High Priest of our profession, Christ Jesus”. The work of the Lord is the profession of the called, the true calling over any occupation held in Babylon. Pharaoh called Israel idle for wanting to go and sacrifice to their God; the words he called vain are the calling.

precepts.text: Harden not your hearts as in the provocation in the wilderness; take heed, brethren, lest there be in any of you an evil heart of unbelief in departing from the living God.
precepts.point: The little ones they said would be a prey, those He would bring into the land; but the children would wander in the wilderness forty years, a year for each of the forty days the land was searched, and bear the whoredoms of their fathers until their carcasses were wasted. The very men that brought up the evil report died by the plague before the Lord, but Joshua and Caleb lived still.

note.label: Numbers 14: The Congregation Rebels and Is Condemned

precepts.why:
The children would “wander in the wilderness forty years”, a year for each of the forty days the land was searched, “until your carcases be wasted in the wilderness.” Hebrews calls that generation by name.

“Harden not your hearts, as in the provocation, in the day of temptation in the wilderness: When your fathers tempted me, proved me, and saw my works forty years. Wherefore I was grieved with that generation, and said, They do alway err in their heart; and they have not known my ways. So I sware in my wrath, They shall not enter into my rest.” The oath of Numbers 14, that they should not come into the land, is the oath that they shall not enter into His rest.

“Take heed, brethren, lest there be in any of you an evil heart of unbelief, in departing from the living God.” The provocation in the wilderness was an evil heart of unbelief, and the warning is to us, that we harden not our hearts as they did.

precepts.text: Some when they had heard did provoke, and he was grieved with them forty years in the wilderness.
precepts.point: Israel became a burden to Moses to the point he asked the Most High to kill him rather than let him see his own wretchedness. While I am yet alive with you this day, ye have been rebellious against the Lord; and how much more after my death?

note.label: Deuteronomy 31: Moses' Final Charge and the Rebellion Foretold

precepts.why:
“For some, when they had heard, did provoke: howbeit not all that came out of Egypt by Moses. But with whom was he grieved forty years? was it not with them that had sinned, whose carcases fell in the wilderness?” All forty years in the wilderness Moses was grieved. Every day there was some issue, some drama the children of Israel raised, and the ones that provoked left their carcases in the wilderness.

We think we grieve dealing with a congregation of a few hundred. Moses dealt with the rebellious spirits of all twelve tribes, thousands upon thousands, for forty years. That is why he could say I know thy rebellion and thy stiff neck: ye have been rebellious against the Lord while I am yet alive, and how much more after my death?

points: Exhort one another daily, while it is called To day. How do you exhort your wife daily? Exhorting is encouraging one to do what is right. Some of you wake up, leave for nine or ten hours, come back, shower, go to Care 101, and the whole relationship with your wife is, hey, what's up though. Five words a day, while you are on Telegram getting on brothers about how we have to communicate.

From the index cards the women fill out in different congregations, leadership hears things that do not make sense: a husband that does not even want his wife to say good morning to him. There was a brother who demanded his wife read chapters every day, come up with ten questions a day for him, while she was homeschooling their five or six kids and he was never there. You do not even do that yourself. That is a militant mindset about our household, and it comes from fear, misplaced anger, and thinking we have to rule our houses with ego.

If you do not teach your wife, you are not teaching your daughters, and you are not teaching your sons. You get a breakdown, an epiphany, something off the chain, and you do not tell your wife. Then she misreads a scripture and gets embarrassed, or she quotes Bishop, a captain, an officer, a mother in the truth, because that is the only biblical words she hears. When she references things, she references the people she hears teaching the Bible. She should hear you teaching the Bible. Why not?

Harden not your hearts, as in the provocation. Paul takes us right back to the history we just read: with whom was he grieved forty years? them whose carcases fell in the wilderness. And to whom sware he that they should not enter into his rest, but to them that believed not?

points: Exhort one another daily, while it is called To day; lest any of you be hardened through the deceitfulness of sin. You get hardened because you have been in the sin so long you start to think that is the only way. No: God's laws are the way.

Psychological note read from the book: the concept of emotional triggers as conditioned responses was advanced by trauma researchers including Peter Levine (Waking the Tiger, 1997), who described how the nervous system stores unresolved traumatic experiences and reactivates them in response to environmental cues.

points: So the scripture says, be mindful, lest there be any of you that have an evil heart of unbelief. You mean to tell me you can walk in this truth, you can be coming to the school every Sabbath day, and be walking around with an evil heart of unbelief?

In departing from the living God. Because throughout my years — my few years in this truth — I am telling you, people leave spiritually long before they leave physically. People leave the truth and leave the body spiritually well before they leave physically.

note.label: Resetting Your Joy In The Lord

points: But exhort one another daily, while it is called To day. While it is called today. When it says to depart from God, what does that mean?

note.label: Resetting Your Joy In The Lord

points: But with whom was the Lord grieved forty years? Was it not with them that had sinned? It was with them that had sinned — with the Israelites that had sinned in the wilderness.
Whose carcases fell in the wilderness. Who dropped dead in the wilderness.

You know, a lot of times — remember what Solomon said. Read that in Ecclesiastes 8. Solomon said something very heavy. Because this said, but with whom was he grieved forty years? And then they dropped dead.

note.label: Resetting Your Joy In The Lord

points: And to whom sware he that they should not enter into his rest, but to them that believed not? So who did the Lord say was not going to enter into his rest? Those that continue to sin — they would not enter into his rest.
What are some of the sins that the children of Israel were committing in the wilderness?

note.label: Resetting Your Joy In The Lord

points: And to whom sware he that they should not enter into his rest, but to them that believed not? But to them that believed not.

So the Lord is telling us to go back and look at the example of our forefathers, and look at the spirits that they were dealing with. They could not enter into the rest at that time, which is the land of Canaan. But for our time, it is the kingdom of heaven. It is immortality. It is eternal life.

note.label: Resetting Your Joy In The Lord

points: So we see that they could not enter in because of unbelief. So, guess what? Twenty-three thousand Israelites were not able to enter into the land of Canaan. Why? Because of unbelief. Because of sin and iniquity. Because of murmuring. Because of covetousness. Not being content. Because of sedition.
